title: Chapter 30 — Working Multiple Customers & Floor Craft
intro: The Saturday skill — managing several live customers with grace and team discipline.

sections.title: The Juggling System
sections.content:
Peak traffic means multiple customers at once. The rep who can manage three ups simultaneously outsells the rep who can only handle one — because the one-at-a-time rep loses two.

Customer A is your active — you are presenting or demoing. Stay with them. They are your primary. Do not abandon a customer mid-conversation.

Customer B arrived while you are with A. Make eye contact within 10 seconds. Walk over briefly: 'Welcome in — I am [Name]. I am just finishing up with this customer and I will be right with you. Feel free to look around and I will find you in just a few minutes.' They know they are acknowledged. They will browse and self-qualify.

Customer C arrived while you have A and B. If another rep is available, hand off. If not, quick acknowledgment, name, and time estimate.

sections.title: The Handoff That Works
sections.content:
When you need to help B but A is not ready to close: give A a task. '[Name], I want to make sure you have everything you need. Let me grab the quote specs and I will be right back in about five minutes. Take a closer look at both models and see which one feels right.'

They stay engaged. You help B. Come back and close A.

The critical rule: never let a customer feel abandoned. A 10-second acknowledgment buys you 10 minutes. Silence feels like disrespect.

sections.title: Team Play on Busy Days
sections.content:
On busy days, work with your colleagues. 'I will take the greeting, you jump in if they need product depth.' Splitting the floor is not losing commission — it is serving more customers. The store wins, you both win.

What kills you: trying to deeply serve three people at once. You cannot. Triage — who is closest to buying? Give them priority. Who is browsing? Acknowledge and queue. Who needs a specialist? Hand off to the right person.
